verdict: Computex blockbuster: MRVL +32% on NVIDIA 'next trillion-dollar company' call + $2B investment; COHR +17%; NVDA +6%; HBM pricing to surge multiples in 2027 per TrendForce; AVGO AI record but guides light.
body_md:
## Fresh developments (last 24–72h)

**Computex 2026 (June 1–4) dominates this entire period.**

**MRVL +32% — MUST-CATCH:** At Computex on June 2, Jensen Huang appeared onstage with Marvell CEO Matthew Murphy, declared Marvell "the next trillion-dollar company," and announced a **$2B NVIDIA investment** enabling semi-custom AI system development. MRVL surged 32% June 2, extended ~+10% premarket June 3; up >237% YTD in 2026. Market cap ~$250B. Exactly the NVIDIA-names-a-partner catalyst flagged in the watchlist.

**NVDA +6% (June 1–2):** Huang unveiled Vera Rubin rack-scale solutions ramping to full production and the RTX Spark "superchip" (Blackwell GPU + N1X CPU) for PCs in partnership with Microsoft, Dell, HP, ASUS, Lenovo, MSI. Goldman reiterated Buy/$285; Morgan Stanley turned more bullish.

**COHR +17.4% (June 2):** Computex optical connectivity comments sent COHR from mid-$320s to ~$423. Q3 FY26 (May 6): record revenue, 6-inch InP ramp ahead of schedule, $2B NVIDIA LTA intact. Raymond James raised PT to $371 (Strong Buy).

**AVGO Q2 FY2026 (June 2):** AI semiconductor revenue $10.8B (+143% YoY); total revenue $22.19B (+48% YoY) — record. BUT software missed ($7.18B vs $7.32B est.) and Q3 consolidated guidance of $29.4B / AI $16B landed below aggressive buy-side models. Stock –7% to –13% after hours.

**CRDO Q4 FY2026 (June 1):** Revenue $1.34B (+206% YoY); FY2027 guidance +80% with optical >$600M. Roth $300 PT, Mizuho $290, JPM $250.

**HIVE +10.3% (June 1):** Announced 320MW AI "Gigafactory" in Greater Toronto Area (100K NVIDIA GPU capacity). First liquid-cooled B200 cluster live with Bell Canada, contributing ~$15M ARR; contracted HPC ARR now ~$35M.

**MU +5% (June 1):** Zacks reinstated Strong Buy ("Bull of the Day"). Q3 earnings expected ~June 24. HBM demand still exceeds supply (fulfilling only ~60% of requests); stock +162% in 2026.

**TrendForce HBM/DRAM (June 1–2):** DRAM industry revenue +81% QoQ in Q1-2026 confirmed. Q2 conventional DRAM +58–63% QoQ, NAND +70–75% QoQ. Critically: HBM contract prices **"expected to surge multiples higher in 2027"** as suppliers negotiate HBM4 agreements in Q2-2026. Note: HBM profitability fell below DDR5 64GB RDIMM since Q1-2026, incentivizing suppliers to sharply reprice HBM4.

**FSLR:** Section 232 polysilicon tariff decision expected by end of June — still a pending catalyst.

## Context vs baseline

- **Correction-after-2026 risk:** TrendForce's June 2 note tilts against near-term correction — suppliers are using HBM4 annual negotiations to recapture suppressed margins, with 2027 prices forecast multiples higher. Long-term supply expansion risk (late 2026) unchanged.
- **Hyperscaler capex:** Now tracking $725B for Big 4 in 2026, above the $600–700B baseline. No guide-downs.
- **NVIDIA dominance:** Computex reinforced platform lock-in (Vera Rubin, RTX Spark, MRVL partnership), consistent with $350B revenue consensus.

---

## Most important development

**MRVL +32% on Jensen Huang's "next trillion-dollar company" call** — backed by a $2B NVIDIA investment — is the defining catalyst of this period and the archetype must-catch event described in the watchlist brief. The secondary wave (COHR +17%, NVDA +6%, HIVE +10%) confirms Computex as a broad AI-infrastructure bull catalyst. AVGO's after-hours drop on a software/guidance miss is the lone cautionary note amid an otherwise strongly bullish session.
